questions.explanation_text: (A) Hydrogen reacts with carbon monoxide in presence of cobalt catalyst to give methanol $2H_{2}(g)+CO(g)\overset{\text{cobalt catalyst}}{\longrightarrow}CH_{3}OH(I)$ (B) Syn gas is produced from coal and the process is called coal gasification. $C(s)+H_{2}O(g)\overset{1270K}{\longrightarrow}\underset{(\text{syn gas)}}{CO(g)+H_{2}(g)}$ (C) Reaction of steam with hydrocarbons or coke at high temperature in presence of nickel catalyst gives a mixture of $CO$ and $H_{2}$ , called water gas $CH_{4}(g)+H_{2}O(g)\underset{Ni}{\overset{1270K}{\longrightarrow}}\underset{(\text{water gas})}{CO(g)+3H_{2}(g)}$ (D) Electrolysis of brine solution produces $H_{2}$ gas at cathode and $Cl_{2}$ gas at anode $NaCl(aq) \longrightarrow Na^{+}(aq)+Cl^{-}(aq)$ Cathode : $2H_{2}O(l)+2e^{-} \longrightarrow H_{2}(g)+2OH^{-}(aq)$ Anode : $2Cl^{-}(aq) \longrightarrow Cl_{2}(g)+2e^{-}$
questions.explanation_html:
(A) Hydrogen reacts with carbon monoxide in presence of cobalt catalyst to give methanol

$2H_{2}(g)+CO(g)\overset{\text{cobalt catalyst}}{\longrightarrow}CH_{3}OH(I)$

(B) Syn gas is produced from coal and the process is called coal gasification.

$C(s)+H_{2}O(g)\overset{1270K}{\longrightarrow}\underset{(\text{syn gas)}}{CO(g)+H_{2}(g)}$

(C) Reaction of steam with hydrocarbons or coke at high temperature in presence of nickel catalyst gives a mixture of $CO$ and $H_{2}$ , called water gas

$CH_{4}(g)+H_{2}O(g)\underset{Ni}{\overset{1270K}{\longrightarrow}}\underset{(\text{water gas})}{CO(g)+3H_{2}(g)}$

(D) Electrolysis of brine solution produces $H_{2}$ gas at cathode and $Cl_{2}$ gas at anode

$NaCl(aq) \longrightarrow Na^{+}(aq)+Cl^{-}(aq)$

Cathode : $2H_{2}O(l)+2e^{-} \longrightarrow H_{2}(g)+2OH^{-}(aq)$

Anode : $2Cl^{-}(aq) \longrightarrow Cl_{2}(g)+2e^{-}$
